local_articles.title: Fallout over Rohit Sharma, clashes with VVS Laxman and England review meeting snub led to Ajit Agarkar's exit: Report
local_articles.snippet: Ajit Agarkar is set to end his tenure as chairman of selectors of the men's national cricket team. It has now come to light that a fallout over the future of former India captain Rohit Sharma proved to be a primary catalyst behind Agarkar parting ways with the BCCI ahead of the ODI World Cup 2027, according to a report by PTI. The trouble started just before the white-ball series against England. The selection committee, headed by Ajit Agarkar, and in agreement with the team management, decided to move on from Rohit Sharma in ODIs after the match at Lord's. A collective decision was taken, and South Zone selector Pragyan Ojha, one of Rohit's closest friends, was asked to communicate the call to him. Rohit Sharma, who is eager to play in the ODI World Cup 2027, was far from happy. He reached out to a top administrator from BCCI to express his disappointment over how he was being treated.

local_articles.title: Three ICC trophies, tough calls and a commitment to fairness: Ajit Agarkar goes out with reputation enhanced
local_articles.snippet: a one-sided final at Ahmedabad. Agarkar’s modus operandi was clear. Don’t prep months before an important event. Rather plan from one event to another. In 2024, after India won the T20 World Cup and Rohit Sharma announced his retirement from the format, Suryakumar Yadav was chosen for captaincy with the 2026 edition in mind. The captain has to be the constant and build the team around him. And he expected his captains to contribute with the bat too. When Suryakumar had a long lean patch, and the X factor had gone out of his batting, he brought in Shreyas Iyer, who had not played T20Is for India for years. It’s not easy to drop a World Cup-winning captain, but Agarkar kept his emotions in check and opted for a captain who was also likely to do well as a batsman till the next event. questions.title: Who will be the first person charged in the United Kingdom over alleged involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide?
questions.background: British authorities have been investigating allegations involving Rwandan genocide suspects living in the United Kingdom.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official public charging announcement from the United Kingdom’s Crown Prosecution Service. Resolution : Identify the first individual formally charged in the United Kingdom in connection with alleged involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide, provided the charges are announced by December 31, 2026. Arrests without charges, extradition proceedings, and charges brought outside the United Kingdom do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The person’s full name as given in the charging announcement.
questions.current_reasoning: Scotland Yard's War Crimes Team has investigated six Rwandan genocide suspects in the UK since 2018 and confirmed in December 2025 that two investigations are at an advanced stage with full files submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service (one submitted in late 2023, a second by late 2025), while none had been charged as of May 2026. The two CPS files almost certainly come from the four named suspects interviewed voluntarily in 2020—Celestin Mutabaruka (Kent), Celestin Ugirashebuja (Essex), Emmanuel Nteziryayo (Manchester), and Dr. Vincent Bajinya, who legally changed his name to Vincent Brown (London)—whereas fifth suspect Charles Munyaneza (Bedford) suffered a stroke and was only interviewed in 2024, and a sixth suspect arrested in Gateshead in January 2024 remains publicly unnamed. Splitting Bajinya's ~20% share between his UK legal name 'Vincent Brown' (11%) and birth name 'Vincent Bajinya' (9%) reflects CPS charging announcement naming conventions while leaving 19% for Munyaneza and unnamed suspects.

questions.title: Which former minister from Viktor Orban's government, if any, will have parliamentary immunity lifted in September 2026 to permit an embezzlement investigation?
questions.background: The party that won Hungary's 2026 parliamentary election campaigned on tackling corruption. Parliamentary immunity can prevent prosecutors from pursuing criminal investigations against legislators unless Parliament lifts it.

Allegations alone, without the parliamentary vote, do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the former minister's full name. If no former minister qualifies during September 2026, resolve as no qualifying minister.

questions.title: Which activist detained in Tunisia's Global Sumud Flotilla fundraising case will suspend his hunger strike between September 12 and September 27, 2026?
